answer: Behavioural kin clustering: each seat commits a signed trace of 200 task outputs per epoch, and the verifier embeds them and merges any seats with pairwise similarity above 0.8 into one cluster that earns a single reward slot. A vault of commitments, sealed before the epoch, stops traces being edited afterwards. An anchor set of known-independent agents fixes the baseline, and sparse tundra regions of embedding space get the highest weight. 500 fakes need 100,000 distinct outputs per epoch, paid whether caught or not.
